messages:
Mira: Heads-up: dashboards showing p50/p95 healthy but p99 in EU endpoint is spiking ~300ms after yesterday's rollout. Not seeing same in us-west.
Diego: Which dashboard? per-endpoint pctl? screenshot?
Mira: /console -> Latency > endpoint breakdown -> /v1/chat EU region. Screenshot attached in thread (link) but short version: p50 ~80ms, p95 ~160ms, p99 jumped to 520ms.
Priya: Was there any routing change targeting eu region? infra-bot shows a rollout for regional-fallbacks at 6165430500 yesterday evening.
infra-bot: Rollout event: regional-fallbacks v3 applied -> enable eu->global-fallback for low-capacity (started 6165430500)
Omar: Two hypotheses: 1) sample tagging differs (some EU requests marked as 'global' origin so aggregated incorrectly), 2) different node pool in EU has higher tail. Need to split percentiles by origin and pool to confirm.
Mira: I ran a quick log-sample: some requests from eu-west-1 had sample_origin=\"router_global\" while they should be \"local_router\". That would route them into the global rollup and change aggregation mix.
Diego: If sample_origin label flips, dashboard rollups might combine different latency distributions -> p99 jump is plausible. Can we query raw events? Suggest: `SELECT region, sample_origin, pool_id, p50(lat_ms), p95(lat_ms), p99(lat_ms) FROM request_events WHERE endpoint='/v1/chat' AND ts>now()-6h GROUP BY region, sample_origin, pool_id`
Priya: Ran similar and saw ~12% of eu requests mislabeled as router_global from 6159800000->6165431000 window. The marking started coincident with the rollout.
Omar: So rollout likely added a codepath that sets origin incorrectly when fallback executes. Two fixes: 1) quick rollback of fallback for eu (canary revert), 2) patch router to preserve origin tag and reprocess recent rollup windows.
Mira: UI/UX note: customers see p99 spike in console but p95 looks fine -> we should add inline explanation when p99 diverges from p95+p50 (tooltip) explaining sampling/rollup caveats. ui-bot can you file a small UX ticket?
ui-bot: Creating ticket: CON-721 add pctl divergence tooltip + split-by-origin toggle on endpoint view. Will link PR.
Diego: Operationally: Omar, can you and infra team coordinate a canary revert for regional-fallbacks in eu for 30min to confirm it's the cause? Also create a metric alert for origin-change-rate>1% to catch this earlier.
Omar: Scheduling canary revert now, will throttle to avoid client impact. Will also add alert: `alert: sample_origin_flip_rate` threshold=1% window=15m. Started at 6165432130
infra-bot: Canary revert: regional-fallbacks v3 -> disabled for region=eu (started 6165432130)
Priya: After revert, p99 dropped ~260ms within ~6 minutes for the eu endpoint. Looks like revert helped.
Mira: Good. Next: patch router to keep original origin when invoking fallback and add unit test. Omar/Priya to own. Diego to add dashboard rollup acceptance test to CI so rollouts can't introduce origin-tag regressions.
Omar: Will open infra PR with fix + tests. Also proposing a backfill job to recompute aggregation for the affected 6h window if we want historical accuracy.
Diego: Backfill ok but keep it opt-in for cost reasons. File a ticket for backfill with estimated tokens.
Mira: Action items recap: revert done (Omar), origin bugfix PR (Omar/Priya), dashboard CI check (Diego), UI tooltip + toggle (ui-bot), backfill ticket (Mira). Thanks all.
Priya: Also adding note: avoid exposing pool_id in top-level legends by default (use top3 + other) to keep dashboards readable.
Mira: Agreed. We'll follow same pattern as other endpoint views.
Diego: Thanks team. Follow-up in #eng-platform tomorrow for PR reviews. :white_check_mark:
